guarantees.claim: reg_state_valid is 0 unless mux_sel_buf_output equals SelSw and lc_ctrl_pkg::lc_tx_test_false_strict(lc_escalate_en_i) is true, in which case it equals keccak_state_valid_i.
When mux_sel_buf_output == SelSw and lc_escalate not active, and keymgr_key_en_i is low, reg_state_o is assigned directly from keccak_state_i.

When the outer condition holds and keymgr_key_en_i is high, for each share i from 0 to Share-1, reg_state_o[i] is partially zeroed: if reg_keccak_strength_i is L128/L224/L256/L384/L512, the corresponding capacity bits (high KeccakBitCapacity bits) are zeroed; for any other strength (default branch), the entire reg_state_o[i] is zeroed.
guarantees.cond: mux_sel_buf_output == SelSw && lc_escalate not active && keymgr_key_en_i == 1

guarantees.claim: If mux_sel_buf_output != SelSw or lc_escalate is active, reg_state_o is forced to all zeros.

assumptions.claim: keccak_state_i and keccak_state_valid_i must be stable and correctly represent the Keccak state while mux_sel_buf_output == SelSw and lc_escalate is not active.
assumptions.cond: when outer condition true and keymgr_key_en_i low
assumptions.risk: Glitches or invalid keccak state could propagate to reg_state_o and reg_state_valid, causing downstream logic to use corrupt data.

assumptions.claim: KeccakBitCapacity parameter values for L128..L512 must exactly match the actual high-capacity bit-width in keccak_state_i for each strength.
assumptions.risk: Mismatch could leave secret capacity bits unmasked or zero part of the data, compromising security or functionality.

assumptions.claim: keymgr_key_en_i is asserted only when a sideloaded key is used and KMAC is SW initiated; the zeroing logic relies on this intent.
assumptions.risk: If asserted incorrectly (e.g., during HW-initiated mode where the path may differ), the capacity zeroing is unnecessary but harmless; however it indicates a configuration mismatch.

assumptions.claim: lc_escalate_en_i must correctly reflect the lifecycle escalation state so that lc_tx_test_false_strict returns true only when no escalation is active.
assumptions.risk: If escalation is active but the function returns true, keccak state could be output during an escalation event, potentially exposing sensitive state.

uncertain_points.claim: The unique case default branch zeroes all shares when reg_keccak_strength_i does not match any of L128..L512. It is unclear whether this is a deliberate fail‑safe or if the system expects reg_keccak_strength_i to always be within the listed set.
uncertain_points.cond: keymgr_key_en_i high and reg_keccak_strength_i not in {L128,L224,L256,L384,L512}
uncertain_points.risk: If a valid strength is omitted inadvertently, full‑state zeroing could break operation; if an illegal value occurs, masking it with zeros may hide a configuration error.

uncertain_points.claim: When keymgr_key_en_i is low but the outer condition is true, reg_state_o passes keccak_state_i without masking its capacity bits. Need to confirm from higher‑level modules that software cannot read reg_state_o in this case when the Keccak state contains secret capacity (e.g., during non‑sideloaded operations that still produce secrets).
uncertain_points.risk: SW could observe secret capacity bits, leading to a security leak.

uncertain_points.claim: If parameter Share is set to 0, the for loop is skipped and no capacity masking occurs when keymgr_key_en_i is high, exposing the full keccak_state_i (including capacity) to the SW output.
uncertain_points.risk: Direct exposure of secret capacity bits to software, violating security requirements.

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational logic that zeros capacity might produce temporary glitches if reg_keccak_strength_i and keccak_state_i change simultaneously. Although reg_state_valid also tracks keccak_state_valid_i, there is no explicit gating during strength changes.
uncertain_points.cond: Simultaneous change of reg_keccak_strength_i and keccak_state_i while outer condition true
uncertain_points.risk: Downstream logic could sample a transient unzeroed state before the case logic resolves, potentially revealing secrets.

uncertain_points.claim: When lc_escalate is active, reg_state_o is forced to zero and reg_state_valid is deasserted, but no error flag or alert is generated. It is unclear whether consumers can reliably detect this condition or if they could silently use the zeroed data.
uncertain_points.risk: Silent zeroing could mask a security escalation or lead to undetected data corruption.
